idiom_name: hand-written facade header over libzmq (zmq_send/zmq_recv) or rabbitmq-c
implementation_notes: C has no proxies, generics or closures over state, so the gateway is written out by hand: an opaque handle holding the socket and the reply state, plus one function per domain operation, for example inventory_check_stock(gw, sku, &out, err). libzmq supplies only the transport primitive - zmq_send queues a message part and returns immediately - so a request-reply gateway function still has to block on zmq_recv, because a REQ/REP socket is a strict send-then-receive lockstep. What replaces the classic gateway class is the struct-plus-header pair (the handle hides the socket, the header hides nothing of the domain); if any C++ is available in the same build, use the C++ facade instead of hand-rolling the same contract twice.
pitfalls: ZeroMQ strings are length-specified and travel without a trailing NUL, so every received frame must be copied into a NUL-terminated buffer before it is used as a C string.
REQ/REP is a state machine: a second send before the matching recv fails with EFSM and returns -1, so the gateway must own the socket and serialize every call on it.
There is no exception mechanism: each transport call reports failure through a sentinel return and errno, so the domain error type has to be defined and propagated by hand.
Destroying the zmq context while a gateway is alive makes pending calls fail with ETERM; the handle's lifetime must be explicit in the API.
